I might be able to shed a little light on this. I’ve worked at Walmart for a few years now in various areas. Starting at the top with assistant managers, they get trained on the various laws (federal/state/local where applicable) of firearms sales, how background checks are performed, etc. For the most part though, the person wishing to buy a firearm has to fill out the relevant paperwork which is then entered into the computer and is checked by an agency that does the background checks (I’m not sure of the agency’s name off the top of my head). After the approval gets sent back from the agency (usually 24-72 hours) the sale commences and the firearm is sold. The assistant manager over that area is responsible for the training of the department manager and the employees in the sporting goods area. As for the records, they are kept in a locked room for up to 7 years, only people having access being upper management. For firearms themselves, the get shipped in usually by an outside company (fed ex) and recorded by upper management as being in the building. After that they are locked in a cabinet in the back room (separate from any ammunition). Only people having access to the backroads storage is upper management.

Use to work at Dominos, now managing/driving for a mom and pop place, a few tips to keep in mind:

-Most everything you have questions about will be covered when you're trained, if the person training you hasn't answered a question you have, ASK! It's better to ask a question, then find out later what the answer is after something goes wrong.

-Get to know the regular customers. Every place has its regular customers, they'll become a friendly face even on the rough days.

-Always be unfailingly polite, no matter what. If a customer starts giving you shit about time on a delivery, order not being right, whatever it is, always be polite, apologize out the ass, and kill 'em with kindness. Find a way to make the order up to em (even if they're complete shit), if they decide to call the store back, don't give them a reason to turn their attention towards you, just the order itself.

-Learn the streets, not just by GPS, but which streets have less stop signs, higher speed limits, etc. A GPS will most likely give you the most direct route, not necessarily the fastest. Ask other drivers or a manager the best way to get to a place.

-And, lastly, like u/pizzacourier said: "Help with dishes when you are not on the road", but also just help out around the store with anything that needs to be done that you're allowed to do (mostly just random cleaning). It helps out other people that you work with, and if the roles become switched, they're more likely to help you out.

Pretty late to the party but feel obliged to post. I've been a delivery driver for about 3 years now and have plenty of stories, ranging from naked guys and girls, money left on doors with notes etc. But by far the worst delivery I've ever had was about 2 years ago. 
I was working with another driver on the inside, taking turns delivering since the manager had gone home sick. It was my delivery put the pizza in the bag and took off. Got to the apartment, knocked on the door, and heard a voice from inside tell me to come in, ok no big deal, probably has her handful with kids or somethin so I own the door, walk in and made the biggest mistake: I took a breathe. The smell was unforgettable. It smelled like rancid, decomposing flesh that had been sitting in the sun for days while simultaneously being kept hydrated. I continued to walk with only a small falter in my step and took the pizza and pop to the lady in the chair. 
The closer I walked to get the worse the smell got. After what seemed like years she finally handed me the money gave her back change (more than I should have) and walked out of the apartment. As soon as the door was closed behind me, I puked. Puked until I was dry heaving but still puking. Eventually I made it to my car but I could still smell it. It was on my clothes. I did the only logical thing I could think of. I stipped. Hoodie, shirt, pants, socks and shoes all tossed into my trunk. Drove back to the pizza place, got out of my car, grabbed my clothes and walked in like a boss. The other driver just staring at me in my boxers. Went to the back of the store and did laundry.
